name: kvm_s390_set_mem_control
prose: Handles the KVM_S390_VM_MEM_* device attributes by switching on attr->attr. KVM_S390_VM_MEM_ENABLE_CMMA: -ENXIO if !sclp.has_cmma; otherwise, under kvm->lock, -EBUSY if kvm->created_vcpus is nonzero, -EINVAL if kvm->mm->context.allow_gmap_hpage_1m is set, else it sets use_cmma = 1 and use_pfmfi = 0 and returns 0. KVM_S390_VM_MEM_CLR_CMMA: -ENXIO if !sclp.has_cmma, -EINVAL if use_cmma is not set, otherwise it calls s390_reset_cmma(kvm->arch.gmap->mm) under kvm->lock and the srcu read lock and returns 0 (no check of created vcpus). KVM_S390_VM_MEM_LIMIT_SIZE: returns -EINVAL for a ucontrol VM, -EFAULT if reading the u64 at attr->addr fails, -E2BIG if a memory limit is set and the new limit exceeds it, -EINVAL if the new limit is 0; it subtracts 1 from the limit unless it is KVM_S390_NO_MEM_LIMIT, then under kvm->lock, if no vcpus were created, calls gmap_create(current->mm, new_limit): on NULL the result is -ENOMEM, otherwise it removes the old gmap, makes the new one kvm->arch.gmap (private = kvm) and the result is 0; if vcpus exist the result is -EBUSY. This case then logs two VM_EVENT lines (also for the failure results), reading kvm->arch.gmap->asce, and the code does not store the new limit into kvm->arch.mem_limit. Any other attr returns -ENXIO.

name: modify_pagetable
prose: Adds (add true) or removes (add false) kernel page-table mappings for [start, end). It first returns -EINVAL (with WARN_ON_ONCE) if start | end is not page aligned, and again -EINVAL (with WARN_ON_ONCE) if end > __abs_lowcore; these two returns happen before any walk and before the TLB flush. Otherwise it walks the range one pgd entry at a time (pgd_addr_end). With add false it skips empty pgd entries; with add true an empty pgd entry gets a new p4d table from vmem_crst_alloc(_REGION2_ENTRY_EMPTY) (a NULL result goes to out with ret = -ENOMEM) which is installed with pgd_populate. It then calls modify_p4d_table(pgd, addr, next, add, direct, altmap); a nonzero result goes to out and becomes the return value; with add false it then calls try_free_p4d_table. After a complete walk ret is 0. At out, when add is false, it calls flush_tlb_kernel_range(start, end) (also on the error path), and it returns ret. Partial modifications are left in place on an error return. With add false this function itself performs no allocation; whether modify_p4d_table can return an error in that case is determined by that callee (not read).
note: Reviewer 15 (add=false can return -ENOMEM, but removal does no allocation) PARTLY right: vmem.c:444-446 allocation only on add, and ret starts as -ENOMEM only for that goto; a nonzero return with add=false could only come from modify_p4d_table (unread). Prose no longer says -ENOMEM for add=false. Slice cut head; real function at 423-460.

name: vmem_add_mapping
prose: Adds a mapping for [start, start + size) to the vmem area. It reads the mappable range with arch_get_mappable_range() and returns -ERANGE, without taking vmem_mutex, if start is below range.start, if start + size is above range.end + 1, or if start + size wraps around (start + size < start). Otherwise it takes vmem_mutex, calls vmem_add_range(start, size), calls vmem_remove_range(start, size) if that returned nonzero, releases the mutex and returns the result of vmem_add_range (0 on success).
note: Reviewers 1-2 (prose/precondition vs overflow and mutex) consistent with this rewrite: the overflow check and -ERANGE precede mutex_lock (vmem.c:542-547). Contract removed (calls helpers, globals). Slice cut head; real function at 537-553.

name: zpci_event_attempt_error_recovery
prose: Tries to recover a PCI function after an error and returns a pci_ers_result_t; it starts with ers_res = PCI_ERS_RESULT_DISCONNECT. It takes device_lock(&pdev->dev) and releases it at out_unlock after calling zpci_report_status(zdev, pdev, "recovery", status_str), so every path ends there. If pdev->error_state is pci_channel_io_perm_failure it skips recovery and returns DISCONNECT. Otherwise it sets pdev->error_state = pci_channel_io_frozen; for a pass-through device, or when no driver is bound or the driver does not support error recovery, it returns DISCONNECT without further steps (no uevent is sent on these paths). It then calls zpci_event_notify_error_detected; if the result indicates abort it returns that value unchanged. If the result is not PCI_ERS_RESULT_NEED_RESET it calls zpci_event_do_error_state_clear and returns that result if it indicates abort. If the current result is NEED_RESET it calls zpci_event_do_reset. A result of PCI_ERS_RESULT_NONE is turned into RECOVERED. If the result is not RECOVERED at that point it sends pci_uevent_ers(DISCONNECT), logs that operator intervention is required, and returns the result as it is (it is not converted to DISCONNECT). Otherwise it logs, calls the driver's resume callback if there is one, sends pci_uevent_ers(RECOVERED) and returns PCI_ERS_RESULT_RECOVERED.
note: Reviewer 1/2 (non-abort votes such as CAN_RECOVER or NEED_RESET can be returned; early skip paths emit no uevent) RIGHT. Reviewer 15 (a failed reset does emit a DISCONNECT uevent; NEED_RESET from error_detected triggers a reset instead of being returned) RIGHT: pci_event.c:235-236,248-253. Slice cut head; real function at 179-265.

name: zpci_directed_irq_init
prose: Init function for directed PCI interrupts. It creates zpci_sbv with airq_iv_create(num_possible_cpus(), 0, NULL) and returns -ENOMEM if that fails. It then fills a zeroed union zpci_sic_iib (isc = PCI_ISC, nr_cpus = num_possible_cpus(), disb_addr = physical address of zpci_sbv->vector) and calls zpci_set_irq_ctrl(SIC_IRQ_MODE_DIRECT, 0, &iib), ignoring its result. It allocates zpci_ibv with kcalloc(num_possible_cpus(), ...) and returns -ENOMEM if that fails. For each possible CPU it creates zpci_ibv[cpu] with airq_iv_create (cache_line_size() * BITS_PER_BYTE bits, flags AIRQ_IV_DATA | AIRQ_IV_CACHELINE, plus AIRQ_IV_ALLOC for CPU 0) and returns -ENOMEM if one fails. On all three -ENOMEM returns it does not free or undo the earlier allocations or the SIC setting. On success it runs cpu_enable_directed_irq on all CPUs with on_each_cpu(..., 1), sets zpci_irq_chip.irq_set_affinity = zpci_set_irq_affinity and returns 0.
note: Reviewers concerned the old formal contract and ENOMEM; prose now lists the exact -ENOMEM sites and the lack of cleanup (pci_irq.c:449-474). Contract removed (globals). Slice cut head; real function at 444-480.

name: zpci_irq_init
prose: Init function for PCI interrupt handling. It sets irq_delivery to DIRECTED if sclp.has_dirq is set, else FLOATING, and forces FLOATING when s390_pci_force_floating is set; if DIRECTED it sets zpci_airq.handler = zpci_directed_irq_handler. It calls register_adapter_interrupt(&zpci_airq) and returns that result if nonzero. Otherwise it sets *zpci_airq.lsi_ptr = 1, calls zpci_floating_irq_init() (FLOATING) or zpci_directed_irq_init() (DIRECTED); if that returns nonzero it calls unregister_adapter_interrupt(&zpci_airq) and returns the error. On success it calls zpci_set_irq_ctrl(SIC_IRQ_MODE_SINGLE, PCI_ISC, &iib) with a zeroed iib (result ignored) and returns 0.
note: Reviewers asked for the negative returns of the two init helpers and cleanup: stated (pci_irq.c:511-539). Contract removed. Slice cut head; real function at 499-540.

name: sh7343se_devices_setup
prose: Init function for the SH7343 SolutionEngine board devices. It stores irq_find_mapping(se7343_irq_domain, SE7343_FPGA_IRQ_UARTA) into serial_platform_data[0].irq, the mapping for SE7343_FPGA_IRQ_UARTB into serial_platform_data[1].irq, and the mapping for SE7343_FPGA_IRQ_USB into both usb_resources[2].start and .end (irq_find_mapping can return 0 for an unmapped hwirq, which is stored as is). It then returns platform_add_devices(sh7343se_platform_devices, ARRAY_SIZE(...)), the value of that call unchanged: 0 on success, or the error from the first platform_device_register failure, in which case platform_add_devices unregisters all devices registered earlier in that call (it loops while (--i >= 0)).
note: Reviewer 2 (platform_add_devices only unregisters the failed device) WRONG and reviewer 15 (it unregisters all previously registered devices) RIGHT: drivers/base/platform.c:508-514 loops while (--i >= 0) platform_device_unregister(devs[i]). Code at setup.c:147-159. Slice cut head.

name: heartbeat_timer
prose: Timer callback for the SH heartbeat LED driver. It recovers hd (struct heartbeat_data) from the timer with timer_container_of, then calls heartbeat_toggle_bit(hd, bit, hd->flags & HEARTBEAT_INVERTED), where bit and up are function-static variables (initially 0 and 1) shared by all instances. heartbeat_toggle_bit does not toggle: it sets the LED register bits to the single bit (1 << hd->bit_pos[bit]) (or its complement when inverted), masked with hd->mask, preserving the bits outside hd->mask. The callback then does bit += up and negates up if bit is 0 or bit == hd->nr_bits - 1, and re-arms the timer with mod_timer(&hd->timer, jiffies + (110 - ((300 << FSHIFT) / ((avenrun[0] / 5) + (3 << FSHIFT))))). The code does not check nr_bits or the index range; with hd->nr_bits of 1, or if bit already equals nr_bits - 1 while up is 1, bit moves outside 0..nr_bits-1.
note: Reviewers: 'nr_bits=1 makes index go out of bounds' RIGHT, 'it sets or clears, not toggles' RIGHT (the helper writes a fixed pattern), 'bit = nr_bits-1 with up=1 advances out of range' RIGHT. Code at heartbeat.c:32-72. Slice cut head.
